q: The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act applies to establishments employing:

options.B: 20 or more workmen as contract labour on any day of the preceding 12 months

q: The Act does NOT apply to establishments where the work is:

options.B: Of an intermittent or casual nature

q: Work is of an "intermittent" nature if performed for:

options.A: More than 120 days in the preceding 12 months
options.B: Less than 120 days in the preceding 12 months

q: "Contract labour" under Section 2(b) means a workman hired:

options.A: In connection with the work of an establishment by or through a contractor
options.B: Directly by the principal employer

q: Every principal employer of a covered establishment must:

options.B: Obtain a certificate of registration under Section 7

q: Registration of the establishment is granted by the:

options.B: Registering officer appointed under the Act

q: Registration of a principal employer may be revoked if:

options.B: It was obtained by misrepresentation or the employer breached conditions

q: A contractor must obtain a licence under Section 12 when he employs:

options.B: 20 or more contract labour

q: A contractor's licence is granted by the:

options.B: Employer

q: A licence may be suspended or revoked under Section 14 if the contractor:

options.B: Fails to comply with licence conditions

q: The contractor must display a copy of the licence:

options.B: Prominently at the place of work

q: The security deposit furnished by the contractor is for:

options.B: Due performance of licence conditions including wage payment

q: Canteen facilities must be provided by the contractor where contract labour numbering:

options.B: 100 or more is ordinarily employed

q: Rest rooms or alternative accommodation must be provided where contract labour is:

options.A: Required to halt at night in connection with the work
options.B: On day shift

q: The contractor must provide at the work site:

options.B: Drinking water, latrines, urinals and washing facilities

q: First-aid facilities at the work site must include:

options.B: A readily accessible first-aid box with prescribed contents

q: If the contractor fails to provide amenities, the principal employer:

options.B: Must provide them within the prescribed time and recover the cost from the contractor
options.D: Must pay a fine to the union

q: Responsibility for payment of wages to contract labour lies primarily with the:

options.B: Contractor

q: Wages must be paid by the contractor:

options.B: In the presence of the principal employer's authorised representative

q: If the contractor fails to pay wages, the principal employer:

options.B: Must pay the wages and recover the amount from the contractor

q: The Central Advisory Contract Labour Board is constituted by the:

options.B: Central Government

q: State Advisory Contract Labour Boards are constituted to advise:

options.B: The State Government

q: The appropriate government may prohibit employment of contract labour in any process or operation under:

options.B: Section 7

q: Before prohibiting contract labour, the government must consider whether the work is:

options.B: Of perennial nature and done ordinarily through regular workmen

q: Abolition of contract labour in an establishment results in:

options.A: Automatic absorption of contract workers as regular employees in all cases
options.B: The principal employer engaging work directly; absorption depends on law and facts

q: Inspectors appointed under the Act may:

options.B: Enter premises, examine registers and take evidence

q: Obstructing an inspector is punishable with:

options.A: Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs 500 or both
options.B: Death penalty

q: Contravention of the Act's provisions is punishable with:

options.A: Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs 1,000 or both
options.B: Only a warning

q: For a continuing contravention, an additional fine of up to:

options.B: Rs 10,000 per day

q: Offences by companies make liable:

options.B: Every person in charge of and responsible for the conduct of business

q: The contractor must maintain registers showing:

options.B: Persons employed, wages paid and deductions

q: The principal employer must maintain a register of:

options.B: Only permanent staff

q: A workman is deemed "contract labour" even if hired:

options.B: Without the knowledge of the principal employer

q: Railway establishments engaging contractors for perennial works like track maintenance:

options.B: Must comply with registration, licensing and amenity provisions
options.D: Are covered only by the Railways Act

q: The licence granted to a contractor is valid ordinarily for:

options.B: The period specified, usually up to 12 months, renewable

q: Where 50 women contract labour are employed, the contractor must provide:

options.B: A cinema

q: Deductions from wages of contract labour are governed by:

options.A: The Payment of Wages Act principles applied through the Rules
options.B: The contractor's discretion

q: Overtime wages for contract labour must be paid at:

options.B: Double the ordinary rate

q: The appropriate government for a railway establishment under this Act is the:

options.B: Central Government

q: Weekly holiday for contract labour is:

options.B: One day of rest per week

q: The normal working hours for adult contract labour are:

options.B: 8 hours a day with prescribed rest intervals

q: Employment of a contractor without a licence where required renders the principal employer:

options.B: Liable to prosecution under the Act

q: The certificate of registration specifies:

options.A: The nature of work for which contract labour may be employed
options.B: The contractor's caste

q: An appeal against revocation of registration lies to:

options.A: The appellate officer designated by the government
options.B: The civil court

q: The Act's welfare provisions apply:

options.B: To all contract labour irrespective of sex

q: "Principal employer" under Section 2(g) in relation to railways means:

options.B: The head of the department or the authority specified by the Central Government

q: Notice of commencement and completion of contract work must be given by:

options.B: The principal employer and the contractor to the inspector

q: The Act came into force on:

options.B: 10th February 1971

q: Which of the following is a core consideration for abolition of contract labour?

options.A: Whether the work is of perennial nature and done by regular workmen in similar establishments
options.B: The contractor's profit margin

q: After abolition is notified for a process, engaging contract labour there is:

options.B: Prohibited and punishable
